maximum_pilot.reason: Findings justify shadow/offline experiments only; no independently validated low-risk forecasting mutation clears promotion gates.

source.title: A market-calibrated accelerated failure time model for in-play football forecasting

findings.observed: Across 140 EPL matches evaluated at minute intervals, calibrating continuous-time goal models to kick-off 1X2 and over/under exchange prices was the dominant driver of predictive accuracy; adding time-varying post-shot xG supplied in-play information.
findings.derived: ARGUS should treat pre-match market probabilities as a strong prior carried into LIVE, then update only with timestamp-valid in-play evidence. This supports market-anchored residual modelling rather than trying to relearn all team strength independently in LIVE.
findings.hypothesis: A market-anchored LIVE residual model will improve Brier/log-loss and abstention quality over the current LIVE baseline without increasing stale-state failures.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Shadow-only replay: at each historical minute snapshot, compare current LIVE probability to a version anchored to de-vigged kick-off market probabilities and updated only from state events with event_time <= decision_time. No staking or production classification changes.
findings.required_evidence: At least 500 matches and 5,000 timestamped LIVE decision snapshots across multiple leagues, with separate evaluation for score changes/red cards and provider-lag periods.
findings.failure_condition: No out-of-sample Brier/log-loss gain, degraded calibration, worse selective-risk curve, or gains disappear when evaluated by league/time block rather than pooled.
findings.rollback: Delete/disable shadow challenger; retain only market-prior diagnostics.
findings.promotion_gate: Maximum Pilot required after independent walk-forward replication.

source.title: A Bayesian bivariate conditional Poisson regression for goal dependence in the English Premier League

findings.observed: A three-season EPL study models home and away goals jointly and reports evidence of negative dependence, using posterior predictive checks for validation.
findings.derived: Independent Poisson scoreline assumptions can be misspecified for exact-score tails and joint outcomes. ARGUS should test dependence-aware scoreline models, but the paper's regressors (attendance, fouls) may not transfer cleanly across leagues or pre-match settings.
findings.hypothesis: A parsimonious dependence-aware score model improves exact-score log score/RPS and 1X2 aggregation versus independent Poisson without harming calibration.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Offline challenger using only features already available before decision time; compare independent Poisson, Dixon-Coles-style adjustment if already present, and a bivariate/dependence-aware alternative on the same folds.
findings.required_evidence: At least 3 full seasons per tested competition or >=2,000 matches total, with league-specific and season-forward evaluation.
findings.failure_condition: Improvement appears only in-sample, requires unavailable/post-event features, worsens 1X2 calibration, or posterior/parameter instability is high.
findings.rollback: Keep existing exact-score model; archive experiment results in failure memory.
findings.promotion_gate: WATCH until multi-league walk-forward evidence exists.

findings.observed: Calibration data should be independent from model-fitting data; isotonic calibration is more prone to overfitting on small datasets and is generally favored only with sufficient sample size (documentation notes roughly >1000 samples).
findings.derived: ARGUS calibration must be fitted strictly out-of-sample and chronologically. Sparse league/market segments should return UNAVAILABLE/SHRUNK rather than force a high-variance calibrator.
findings.hypothesis: Chronologically separated sigmoid/temperature calibration with minimum-sample gates will reduce overconfidence and improve Brier/log-loss without damaging ranking materially.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Offline rolling-origin calibration benchmark: RAW vs sigmoid vs temperature; permit isotonic only in folds meeting minimum sample requirements. Store reliability bins and sample counts alongside metrics.
findings.required_evidence: >=1,000 settled predictions for any isotonic candidate segment; otherwise use simpler calibrators or abstain from segment-specific calibration. Evaluate at least 3 forward folds.
findings.failure_condition: Calibration gain does not persist to next fold, probabilities become more extreme, or selective-risk/CLV worsens despite lower in-sample ECE.
findings.rollback: Restore RAW/previous calibrated probabilities and preserve fold diagnostics.
findings.promotion_gate: No production promotion without forward-fold stability and rollback artifact.

source.title: Forecasting: Principles and Practice — Time series cross-validation

findings.observed: Rolling forecasting origin evaluation restricts each training set to observations available before the forecast origin, preventing future information from entering model construction.
findings.derived: ARGUS model, calibration, abstention, threshold and policy experiments must share one temporal split service keyed by decision_time, not ad-hoc random cross-validation.
findings.hypothesis: A single enforced walk-forward evaluator will surface hidden leakage and reduce false-positive model promotions.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Build/read-only validation manifest that asserts train_max_event_time < evaluation_decision_time for every fold and reports violations without blocking production.
findings.required_evidence: Replay all existing champion/challenger evaluation datasets plus at least one intentionally contaminated fixture to prove the validator catches leakage.
findings.failure_condition: Validator cannot distinguish event_time, ingest_time and decision_time or creates false leakage alarms from legitimate late-arriving settlement data.
findings.rollback: Keep validator report-only; no gating until false-positive rate is acceptably low.
findings.promotion_gate: Low-risk candidate for later Maximum Pilot gating after shadow validation.

findings.observed: The 2026 study formalizes abstention for correlated multi-horizon forecasts and reports improvements over existing abstention baselines across 24 datasets.
findings.derived: ARGUS LIVE should not necessarily use one confidence threshold for every minute/horizon; abstention can be horizon/state-aware. Transfer to football classification is not yet proven.
findings.hypothesis: Minute/horizon-specific abstention thresholds reduce error conditional on action while preserving adequate coverage better than one global threshold.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Paper-shadow risk-coverage curves by horizon bucket (e.g. pre-match, 0-30, 31-60, 61-75, 76+) using existing calibrated probabilities; no new model required initially.
findings.required_evidence: >=5,000 settled decision snapshots with adequate sample in every horizon bucket; report coverage, Brier/log-loss on accepted predictions and missed-opportunity rate.
findings.failure_condition: Coverage collapses, thresholds are unstable across folds/leagues, or gains vanish after accounting for repeated snapshots from the same match.
findings.rollback: Retain global abstention policy and store bucket analysis only.

findings.observed: Prometheus recommends symptom-based paging, actionable alerts, tolerance against transient failures, and instrumentation tied to user-visible outcomes. OpenTelemetry defines common semantic conventions for consistent traces, metrics and logs.
findings.derived: ARGUS Control Plane should distinguish operator-impact symptoms (stale actionable state, broken settlement, unavailable ledger truth) from diagnostic causes, and telemetry fields should use stable names across scheduler/provider/model/settlement paths.
findings.hypothesis: A stable event schema plus symptom-first severity mapping reduces alert noise and shortens root-cause identification without hiding real failures.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Add shadow-normalized telemetry records with fields such as component, operation, match_id, decision_id, event_time, ingest_time, decision_time, freshness_ms, outcome, error_type and severity; do not replace existing alerts initially.
findings.required_evidence: At least 14 days of parallel telemetry and review of all true incidents/false alarms.
findings.failure_condition: New schema loses provenance, creates cardinality/cost problems, or symptom mapping delays a genuine operator-impact incident.
findings.rollback: Stop emitting normalized shadow events; existing alerts remain untouched.
findings.promotion_gate: Maximum Pilot only for changing alert severity/routing, not for shadow telemetry emission.

source.title: FIFA World Cup 2026 contamination-free benchmark for LLM forecasting agents

findings.observed: Across the 2026 World Cup benchmark, none of four frontier LLM forecasting agents beat the pre-match market on Brier score; agents often converged on the same top pick and fading the market was unprofitable for all four.
findings.derived: Free-form LLM match forecasting should not become an ARGUS production probability source or override calibrated market/model probabilities. LLM value is better allocated to failure analysis, hypothesis generation and evidence triage under deterministic governance.
findings.hypothesis: No production forecasting experiment is warranted from this evidence.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: None for production probabilities. If used, restrict LLM to advisory root-cause/hypothesis tasks already permitted by Cognitive Core C1.
findings.required_evidence: Future independently replicated evidence of calibrated incremental value over market/model baseline would be required to revisit.
findings.failure_condition: N/A — rejected due insufficient evidence of transfer/value and governance risk.

findings.observed: As of July 2026, dedicated Brier/ECE calibration metrics were still being proposed/added through open issues, while other open issues report edge-case drift problems and performance concerns at scale.
findings.derived: ARGUS should not introduce Evidently as a new critical dependency merely to compute simple calibration/drift diagnostics that can be implemented deterministically with existing libraries and tests.
findings.hypothesis: A small native metrics layer is lower-risk and cheaper for current ARGUS needs.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: None required before dependency adoption; retain as optional research tooling only.
findings.required_evidence: Revisit only if a concrete missing capability appears and benchmarked operational benefit exceeds dependency/runtime cost.
findings.failure_condition: N/A — dependency expansion rejected for now.
findings.promotion_gate: REJECT for production dependency at this time.
